glosses: The state or fact of being turbulent or agitated; tempestuousness, disturbance.

examples.text: Turbulence was everywhere, within every blade of grass, every drop of dew on a leaf, every cloud in the sky, and every star beyond. The turbulence was purposeless, but in huge quantities of purposeless turbulence, purpose took shape.

glosses: Disturbance in a gas or fluid, characterized by evidence of internal motion or unrest.
Specifically, a state of agitation or disturbance in the air which is disruptive to an aircraft.
An instance or type of such state or disturbance.

examples.text: In a brief and abashed Tory conference speech, Kwarteng admitted it had been a “tough day” – hours after rowing back on the tax cut for high earners. He said his economic plan had caused “a little turbulence”.

glosses: A current of air or water running back, or in an opposite direction to the main current.

examples.text: In the bow old Dobbs fought the stream cunningly, twisting the nose into eddies and backwaters, taking advantage when he could of set of current, and when he could not, paddling doggedly, not so powerfully, perhaps, as his partner, but with equal steadiness.

glosses: A circular current; a whirlpool.

examples.text: And smiling eddies dimpled on the main.
Wheel through the air, in circling eddies play.
It was as though the room were instantly flooded with water. After a moment’s hesitation first one couple, then another, leapt into mid-stream, and went round and round in the eddies.

glosses: To form an eddy; to move in, or as if in, an eddy; to move in a circle.

examples.text: Eddying round and round they sink.

Neither in his voiceless cabin, fragrant with planks of new-cut pine, nor along the lake, nor in the sunset clouds which presently eddied behind the lavender-misted mountains, could Babbitt find the spirit of Paul as a reassuring presence.
It’s a uniquely American news story, one that eddies until it surges, and then, after it has mostly receded from view, surges again.

glosses: A marijuana edible.

examples.text: I never really was into weed until recently. On my "Chrissy Chaos" podcast on Patreon, I do a segment every Friday called the "Chris and Eddy Show" 'cause I call edibles "eddys,' so I take an eddy and I do a show.
These eddies are made with both fruits and veggies, and weed of course, with cozy flavor profiles like honey lemon and apple pie.

If you do end up bringing a couple eddies with you, try removing them from any packaging and passing them off as regular candy. Think ahead of time what dosage of edibles you’d like to bring and how high you’re trying to get.

glosses: An idiosyncrasy; a slight glitch, a mannerism; something unusual about the manner or style of something or someone.

examples.text: The car steers cleanly, but the gearshift has a few quirks.

glosses: An acute angle dividing a molding; a groove that runs lengthwise between the upper part of a molding and a soffit.
A quibble, evasion, or subterfuge.

examples.text: Had you no quirk / To avoid gullage, sir, by such a creature?

Let us not be too curious in prying into Gods arke, leaſt vve ſmart like the flie fluttering about the candle, for God is a conſuming fire to thoſe that vvill be ſporting themſelves in the quirks of their vvit about his ſacred myſteries.

glosses: To (cause to) move with a wry jerk.

examples.text: He quirked an eyebrow.
The corners of her mouth quirked.
He quirked his lips playfully.

glosses: To furnish with a quirk or channel.
To alter in a unique and unusual way.

examples.text: But in the dream the forms are quirked by the peculiar troubles of the dreamer, whereas in myth the problems and solutions shown are directly valid for all mankind.

glosses: To use verbal tricks or quibbles.

examples.text:
I have stung her and wrung her,
The venom is working;—
And if you had hung her
With canting and quirking,
She could not be deader than she will be soon

glosses: Alternative form of querk.

examples.text: „Val und Joe waren viel zu aufgebracht, um Bert mit dem ihm gebührenden Wirbel zu begrüßen, also nahmen Rosa und Bobby es auf sich, ihn im Slalom um die Bücherregale zu jagen.“

examples.text: Sie verursachte einen erheblichen Wirbel in der Versammlung.

examples.text: „Statt weiter zur Küste zu treiben, drehte er sich jetzt in einem Luftwirbel.“

glosses: Mouvement d’un corps qui tourbillonne.

examples.text: Les nuages cessaient de ressembler à des cimes neigeuses ; ils devenaient immatériels et révélaient dans leur contexture un tourbillonnement immense et silencieux.
Une lithographie y représente un pompier qui porte une femme en chemise au sommet d'une échelle dans un tourbillonnement de fumée.
